items.content_html:
This PR adds a NixOS module for ghorg as services.ghorg. ghorg is already packaged in nixpkgs, but it currently lacks declarative configuration through a NixOS module.

The module provides a declarative way to configure and run ghorg reclone jobs on NixOS, including generated per-job config files, optional timer-based execution, and basic service user/data directory management.

The test uses a stub ghorg executable. It intentionally does not exercise real SCM API access or upstream clone behavior, so it remains deterministic and offline.

The test validates the NixOS integration layer:

  • generated systemd service/timer units
  • generated reclone/job config
  • invocation wiring and service execution
  • user/group/data directory setup

items.content_html:
The current documentation regarding TPM2 setup (added in #440251) includes a recommendation to enable the tpm2-abrmd daemon. While tpm2-abrmd could be useful to some NixOS users, the justification in the docs (that it receives updates at a more frequent rate than the Linux kernel) is not very persuasive, as the tpm2-abrmd project has not received any code updates in many years, while the Linux kernel's TPM resource manager has continued to receive updates in that time.

Other Linux distributions that ship with TPM2 support (including immutable OSes such as Fedora Silverblue) do not include the tpm2-abrmd package, so I don't think it makes sense to explicitly recommend it to users without a different reason to do so.

items.content_html:
Add a minimal module profile for lib.nixos.evalModules that produces a bootable NixOS system with 53 modules (and adds a test for that).

A more invasive, but also more thorough take on #401751 et all in a way. We can reduce the resulting module set even further, but I'd prefer to do so iteratively in follow-up PRs. I also have a minimal container profile planned.

lib.nixos.evalModules (with featureFlags.minimalModules) is the experimental entrypoint for evaluating NixOS with an explicit module set - empty even by default - instead of all >1500 modules from module-list.nix. This significantly speeds up evaluation for minimal nixos closures (~25% for the booteable profile) and eases future developments around leaner NixOS closures.

Currently, many modules have hard cross-module dependencies: they read config.services.foo.enable or set services.bar.baz for modules that may not be loaded. With a custom module set this causes evaluation errors.

We make many of those cross-module dependencies optional and add a new minimal/bootable.nix profile, as well as a test for it, to ensure we'll notice future breakage.

Status & dependencies

This PR is ready, it just currently includes its pre-requisites for convenience during review. Only the last commit is intended to be merged here. I'll rebase once each of the following PRs is merged:

  • #507667
  • #507676
  • #507695
  • #507727

items.content_html:
Things done

users.users.<name>.{autoSubUidGidRange,subUidRanges,subGidRanges} are currently only honoured by update-users-groups.pl.
When using services.userborn or systemd.sysusers, /etc/subuid and /etc/subgid are not written at all, which breaks rootless podman and similar (nikstur/userborn#7).

This adds a small Rust tool, nixos-subids, and a nixos-subids.service that takes over the job when either of those backends is enabled.
The perl path is unchanged for now, but I'm planning a follow-up PR to migrate to the new approach unconditionally and remove the perl code for uid and gid mapping entirely.

Differences from the perl allocator:

  • Auto-allocated ranges are checked for overlap against explicitly configured ranges (e.g. the 1e9-wide root range set by the incus module) and skip past them.
    The perl allocator only checks start positions and silently overlaps.
  • Existing entries are never removed, so a range cannot be reassigned to a different owner across generations.
    This mirrors userborn's handling of /etc/passwd.
  • Files are written atomically as regular files, since newuidmap from shadow-utils opens them with O_NOFOLLOW.
  • A new users.subIdRanges.strictOverlapCheck option turns cross-user overlap from a warning into a hard failure before the file is written.
    This is useful to avoid silent security issues on critical systems.

A one-shot nixos-subids-import-legacy.service seeds /etc/sub{u,g}id from /var/lib/nixos/auto-subuid-map on the first run after switching, so allocations made by the perl script survive the migration.
It is gated by ConditionPathExists and is a no-op on fresh installs.

Closes nikstur/userborn#7
See #475305

items.content_html:
The yaml merging logic is taken from

nixpkgs/nixos/modules/services/networking/adguardhome.nix

Lines 179 to 194 in 6201e20

preStart = lib.optionalString (settings != null) ''
if [ -e "$STATE_DIRECTORY/AdGuardHome.yaml" ] \
&& [ "${toString cfg.mutableSettings}" = "1" ]; then
# First run a schema_version update on the existing configuration
# This ensures that both the new config and the existing one have the same schema_version
# Note: --check-config has the side effect of modifying the file at rest!
${lib.getExe cfg.package} -c "$STATE_DIRECTORY/AdGuardHome.yaml" --check-config
# Writing directly to AdGuardHome.yaml results in empty file
${lib.getExe pkgs.yaml-merge} "$STATE_DIRECTORY/AdGuardHome.yaml" "${configFile}" > "$STATE_DIRECTORY/AdGuardHome.yaml.tmp"
mv "$STATE_DIRECTORY/AdGuardHome.yaml.tmp" "$STATE_DIRECTORY/AdGuardHome.yaml"
else
cp --force "${configFile}" "$STATE_DIRECTORY/AdGuardHome.yaml"
chmod 600 "$STATE_DIRECTORY/AdGuardHome.yaml"
fi
'';

items.content_html:
Description

Add a new NixOS module for synchronizing kernel patches from lore.kernel.org.

Features

  • Periodic sync from kernel mailing list archives via public-inbox
  • Support for 14 kernel subsystems:
    • dri-devel - DRM/Graphics
    • netdev - Networking
    • linux-fsdevel - Filesystems
    • linux-mm - Memory management
    • linux-security-module - LSM
    • linux-hardening - KSPP hardening
    • rust-for-linux - Rust kernel development
    • linux-block, linux-btrfs, linux-ext4, linux-xfs - Storage
    • linux-usb, linux-pci - Hardware
  • Optional public-inbox/lei support for full mbox archives
  • Fallback to Atom feeds for lightweight sync
  • Automatic index generation
  • Full systemd hardening (DynamicUser, sandboxing)

Motivation

Kernel developers and security teams need to track upstream patch discussions. This module provides an automated way to sync patches from lore.kernel.org, the official Linux kernel mailing list archive.

Example Usage

Basic setup:

services.lore-sync = {
  enable = true;
  subsystems = [ "linux-hardening" "rust-for-linux" ];
};

Full configuration:

services.lore-sync = {
  enable = true;
  subsystems = [ "dri-devel" "netdev" "rust-for-linux" ];
  interval = "6h";
  lookbackDays = 14;
  useLei = true;  # Use public-inbox for full mbox
};

Use Cases

  • Kernel developers tracking patch discussions
  • Security teams monitoring hardening patches (KSPP)
  • Anyone following Rust-for-Linux development
  • Maintainers tracking filesystem/driver patches

Checklist

  • Module follows nixpkgs conventions
  • Options have descriptions and examples
  • systemd service is hardened (DynamicUser, sandboxing)
  • Added to nixos/modules/module-list.nix
  • Documentation (can add if requested)
  • NixOS test (can add if requested)

Related

  • lore.kernel.org: https://lore.kernel.org/
  • public-inbox: https://public-inbox.org/

Description

Add a new NixOS module for automated CVE synchronization from the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).

Features

  • Periodic CVE data fetching from NVD API 2.0
  • Incremental sync with state tracking (only fetches modified CVEs)
  • CPE-based product filtering (e.g., filter for Linux kernel CVEs only)
  • Automatic kernel CVE extraction for security monitoring
  • Full systemd hardening (DynamicUser, sandboxing, restricted syscalls)
  • Optional API key support for higher rate limits

Motivation

Security-conscious NixOS users and organizations need visibility into CVEs affecting their systems. This module provides the foundation for CVE awareness by fetching authoritative data directly from NIST NVD.

Example Usage

Basic setup:
```nix
services.nvd-sync = {
enable = true;
extractKernelCves = true;
};
```

With API key:
```nix
services.nvd-sync = {
enable = true;
apiKeyFile = config.sops.secrets.nvd-api-key.path;
interval = "hourly";
products = [ "cpe:2.3:o:linux:linux_kernel" ];
};
```

  • systemd service is hardened (DynamicUser, sandboxing)

  • Documentation (can add if requested)

items.content_html:
When an activation occurs that includes a recyclarr config change, this should translate to recylcarr actually applying that change. To do that, I used X-ConfigHash to hash the config, which trigger restarts, along with setting the OnActiveSec to 5s.

I've been running this change on my machine for a while now with no issues.
